<div class="page-shell">

<header class="masthead">
  <div class="eyebrow">WebR practical</div>
  <h1>Odds, log-odds, and odds ratios</h1>
  <p>Follow-up to Intro to Logistic Regression and coefficient interpretation. You will connect probability, odds, and log-odds, then use <code>broom::tidy()</code> with <code>exponentiate = TRUE</code> to read and interpret odds ratios the way papers report them.</p>
</header>

<section class="panel">

<h2>Overview</h2>

<p>In the slide decks you already:</p>

<ul class="tight-list">
  <li>Fitted <code>glm(weak_grip ~ age, family = binomial)</code> on KLOSA data.</li>
  <li>Read the age coefficient <strong>0.117</strong> as a fixed change in <strong>log-odds</strong> per year.</li>
  <li>Saw that papers usually report <strong>odds ratios</strong> instead of raw log-odds.</li>
</ul>

<p>This practical makes those scales concrete in R and gives you practice reading results text.</p>

</section>

<section class="panel">

<h2>Part 1. Four scales for the same chance</h2>

<p>Start with a probability <strong>p</strong>. The other scales follow:</p>

<div class="formula-panel">
$$
\text{odds} = \frac{p}{1-p}, \qquad
\text{log-odds} = \ln(\text{odds}), \qquad
\text{OR from a coef} = e^{\text{log-odds coef}}
$$
</div>

<ul class="tight-list">
  <li><strong>Probability</strong> is between 0 and 1.</li>
  <li><strong>Odds</strong> compare happens vs does-not. Odds = 1 at a 50-50 chance.</li>
  <li><strong>Log-odds</strong> can be any number, balanced around 0. Logistic regression fits here.</li>
  <li><strong>Odds ratio</strong> is what you report: a multiplicative change in odds per unit of the predictor.</li>
</ul>

</section>

<div class="webr-wrap">

<h3>R code: convert between scales</h3>

Try a few probabilities. Run the cell to see odds and log-odds side by side.

```{webr-r}
p <- c(0.10, 0.25, 0.50, 0.75, 0.90)

data.frame(
  probability = p,
  odds = p / (1 - p),
  log_odds = log(p / (1 - p))
)
```

</div>

<div class="practice" data-answer="b">
  <div class="practice-title">Question 1</div>
  <p>At probability <strong>p = 0.50</strong>, what are the odds?</p>
  <div class="choice-set">
<label><input type="radio" name="p0" value="a">Odds = <strong>0.50</strong></label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p0" value="b">Odds = <strong>1</strong> (50-50 means happens and does-not are equal)</label>
  </div>
  <button type="button">Check</button>
  <div class="practice-feedback" data-correct="Correct. 0.50 / 0.50 = 1. A 50-50 chance always has odds of 1." data-incorrect="Not quite. Odds = p / (1 - p). At p = 0.50 that is 0.50 / 0.50 = 1."></div>
</div>

<section class="panel">

<h2>Part 2. Your KLoSA model on the log-odds scale</h2>

<p>Reload the data and refit the age model. The <code>summary()</code> table shows coefficients on the <strong>log-odds</strong> scale.</p>

</section>

<div class="webr-wrap">

<h3>R code: fit the model and read log-odds coefficients</h3>

```{webr-r}
library(dplyr)
library(broom)

klosa <- read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/the-graph-courses/rsr_resources/refs/heads/main/data/28_klosa_men_grip.csv")

grip_model <- glm(weak_grip ~ age, family = binomial, data = klosa)
summary(grip_model)$coefficients
```

</div>

<div class="callout">
<p>The age row <strong>Estimate</strong> (about <strong>0.117</strong>) is the change in <strong>log-odds</strong> of weak grip for each extra year of age. That is the scale <code>glm()</code> uses internally.</p>
</div>

<div class="practice" data-answer="b">
  <div class="practice-title">Question 2</div>
  <p>The age coefficient in <code>summary()</code> is about <strong>0.117</strong>. That number is on which scale?</p>
  <div class="choice-set">
<label><input type="radio" name="p1" value="a">Probability (0 to 1)</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p1" value="b">Log-odds</label>
  </div>
  <button type="button">Check</button>
  <div class="practice-feedback" data-correct="Correct. glm(family = binomial) reports log-odds coefficients by default." data-incorrect="Not quite. The default glm summary is on the log-odds scale, not probability."></div>
</div>

<section class="panel">

<h2>Part 3. Exponentiate to get odds ratios with broom</h2>

<p>To report results like a paper, exponentiate the log-odds coefficients. In R, <code>tidy(..., exponentiate = TRUE)</code> does this for you (it applies <code>exp()</code> to each estimate).</p>

<div class="formula-panel">
$$
\text{OR for age} = e^{0.117} \approx 1.12
$$
</div>

</section>

<div class="webr-wrap">

<h3>R code: tidy with exponentiate = TRUE</h3>

```{webr-r}
tidy(grip_model, exponentiate = TRUE, conf.int = TRUE)
```

</div>

<div class="webr-wrap">

<h3>R code: check the OR by hand</h3>

```{webr-r}
age_or <- exp(coef(grip_model)["age"])
round(age_or, 3)
```

</div>

<div class="practice" data-answer="a">
  <div class="practice-title">Question 3</div>
  <p>In the <code>tidy()</code> output, the <strong>estimate</strong> for <code>age</code> is about <strong>1.12</strong>. What does that mean?</p>
  <div class="choice-set">
<label><input type="radio" name="p2" value="a">Each extra year multiplies the odds of weak grip by about <strong>1.12</strong> (about <strong>12% higher odds</strong>).</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p2" value="b">Each extra year adds <strong>12 percentage points</strong> to the probability of weak grip.</label>
  </div>
  <button type="button">Check</button>
  <div class="practice-feedback" data-correct="Correct. An OR is a multiplicative change in odds. (1.12 - 1) x 100% is about 12% higher odds." data-incorrect="Not quite. The OR changes odds, not probability directly. 1.12 means odds are multiplied by 1.12 each year."></div>
</div>

<section class="panel">

<h2>Part 4. How papers phrase odds ratios</h2>

<p>Authors translate ORs into plain language. Common patterns:</p>

<table class="or-table">
  <thead><tr><th>Odds ratio</th><th>Typical results wording</th></tr></thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr><td>1.12</td><td>12% higher odds</td></tr>
    <tr><td>1.50</td><td>50% higher odds</td></tr>
    <tr><td>2.00</td><td>100% higher odds, or twice the odds</td></tr>
    <tr><td>4.00</td><td>Four times the odds</td></tr>
    <tr><td>0.80</td><td>20% lower odds</td></tr>
    <tr><td>0.50</td><td>50% lower odds, or half the odds</td></tr>
  </tbody>
</table>

<div class="paper-quote">
"Each additional year of age was associated with <strong>12% higher odds</strong> of weak grip (OR 1.12, 95% CI 1.11 to 1.13; p &lt; 0.001)."
</div>

</section>

<div class="practice" data-answer="b">
  <div class="practice-title">Question 4</div>
  <p>A sentence says mothers had <strong>half the odds</strong> of a low birth weight baby. Which OR matches?</p>
  <div class="choice-set">
<label><input type="radio" name="p3" value="a">OR = 1.50</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p3" value="b">OR = 0.50</label>
  </div>
  <button type="button">Check</button>
  <div class="practice-feedback" data-correct="Correct. Half the odds means multiply odds by 0.5." data-incorrect="Not quite. Half the odds is OR = 0.50."></div>
</div>

<section class="panel">

<h2>Part 5. Categorical predictors and reference groups</h2>

<p>When the predictor is a category (age group), R uses the <strong>first level as reference</strong>. Other rows in <code>tidy()</code> are ORs compared to that reference.</p>

</section>

<div class="webr-wrap">

<h3>R code: age groups and ORs vs reference</h3>

```{webr-r}
klosa <- klosa %>%
  mutate(age_group = cut(
    age,
    breaks = c(45, 65, 75, Inf),
    labels = c("45-64", "65-74", "75+"),
    right = FALSE
  ))

group_model <- glm(weak_grip ~ age_group, family = binomial, data = klosa)
tidy(group_model, exponentiate = TRUE, conf.int = TRUE)
```

</div>

<div class="callout">
<p>Typical reading: compared with men aged <strong>45-64</strong> (reference), men aged <strong>65-74</strong> had about <strong>5 times the odds</strong> of weak grip, and men aged <strong>75+</strong> had about <strong>14 times the odds</strong>.</p>
</div>

<div class="practice" data-answer="a">

<label><input type="radio" name="p4" value="b">Men aged <strong>75+</strong></label>
  </div>
  <button type="button">Check</button>
  <div class="practice-feedback" data-correct="Correct. Compared with names the reference. The OR describes the other group relative to it." data-incorrect="Not quite. The reference is named after compared with: men aged 45-64."></div>
</div>

<label><input type="radio" name="p5" value="a">Men 65-74 have <strong>5.22% higher</strong> probability of weak grip.</label>

  </div>

<div class="practice" data-answer="a">
  <div class="practice-title">Question 7</div>
  <p>A table row shows OR = <strong>0.80</strong> (95% CI 0.65 to 0.98) for mother's weight (<code>lwt</code>). Best plain-language reading:</p>

</div>

<section class="panel completion">

<h2>Completion code</h2>

<p>Answer at least 6 out of 7 questions correctly to reveal your completion code.</p>

<p><span id="code-progress">0 of 7 correct (need at least 6)</span></p>

<div class="code-box" id="code-box">
  <div class="code-label">Your completion code</div>
  <div class="code-value" id="code-value"></div>
</div>

</section>

<p class="footer-note">GRAPH Courses practical | Odds, log-odds, and odds ratios</p>

</div>

<script>
const COMPLETION_CODE = "EXPORAT";
const COMPLETION_REQUIRED = 6;

function updateCompletion() {
  const cards = document.querySelectorAll(".practice");
  const correct = document.querySelectorAll(".practice.is-correct").length;
  const total = cards.length;
  const progress = document.getElementById("code-progress");
  const box = document.getElementById("code-box");
  const value = document.getElementById("code-value");

  if (progress) {
    progress.textContent = correct + " of " + total + " correct (need at least " + COMPLETION_REQUIRED + ")";
  }

  if (box && value) {
    if (correct >= COMPLETION_REQUIRED) {
      value.textContent = COMPLETION_CODE;
      box.style.display = "block";
    } else {
      box.style.display = "none";
    }
  }
}

document.querySelectorAll(".practice").forEach((card) => {
  const button = card.querySelector("button");
  const feedback = card.querySelector(".practice-feedback");
  const answer = card.dataset.answer;

  button.addEventListener("click", () => {
    const selected = card.querySelector("input[type='radio']:checked");
    card.classList.remove("is-correct", "is-incorrect");
    card.querySelectorAll("label").forEach((label) => {
      label.classList.remove("correct-choice", "incorrect-choice");
    });

    if (!selected) {
      card.classList.add("is-incorrect");
      feedback.textContent = "Choose an answer first, then check it.";
      updateCompletion();
      return;
    }

    const selectedLabel = selected.closest("label");
    const correctInput = card.querySelector(`input[value="${answer}"]`);
    const correctLabel = correctInput ? correctInput.closest("label") : null;

    if (selected.value === answer) {
      card.classList.add("is-correct");
      selectedLabel.classList.add("correct-choice");
      feedback.textContent = feedback.dataset.correct;
    } else {
      card.classList.add("is-incorrect");
      selectedLabel.classList.add("incorrect-choice");
      if (correctLabel) correctLabel.classList.add("correct-choice");
      feedback.textContent = feedback.dataset.incorrect;
    }

    updateCompletion();
  });
});

updateCompletion();
</script>
